questions.text: What does the shared patch projection do in a Vision Transformer?

options.A: It averages all image patches into one image-level vector.
options.B: It assigns each patch a unique matrix based on its position.
options.C: It maps each flattened patch to a fixed-width token vector.
options.D: It converts each color channel into a separate text token.

questions.explanation: The same learned linear projection maps each flattened patch into the hidden dimension D; positional information is supplied separately.

questions.text: A 224×224 image uses 16×16 patches. With one CLS token and four register tokens, how many tokens enter the vision transformer?
questions.explanation: The 14×14 grid gives 196 patch tokens; adding one CLS and four registers gives 201.

questions.text: In the lesson code, grid_shape rejects image sizes not divisible by patch size. What happens when seq_length receives a config with image_size=384 and patch_size=14?

options.A: It raises ValueError before returning a sequence length.
options.B: It uses a 27×27 grid and discards the remaining pixels.
options.C: It pads the image and uses a 28×28 patch grid.
options.D: It returns 384×384 tokens plus any extra tokens.

questions.explanation: seq_length calls grid_shape, whose divisibility check raises ValueError because 384 % 14 is not zero.
